title: gusto audit.json, version 2
description: The summary at the root of an audit export: who asked, what ran, what changed, which model, what it spent, who approved it, and what the export's policy removed. Every value is derived from the files in the export. Where a value is unknown the field holds one of four words instead: "not recorded" (the platform does not write this down), "redacted" (the export's policy removed it or the file it comes from), "none" (recorded as not happening) or "not measured" (the proxy saw the calls but could not count what they cost). A reader ignores a field it does not know.

version.description: The format of this file. A reader refuses a version newer than it knows.

job.description: The job's ID: the name of its directory.

exportedAt.description: When the export was written, in seconds since the Unix epoch. The one field no file in the export holds.

asked.description: Who asked for the job, from state.json.

who.description: The person who asked. "not recorded" while everybody signs in with one shared password.

how.description: How the job arrived, as state.json's asked field says: the pages or the API. A word in its place when state.json is not in the export.

at.description: When the job was queued, state.json's queuedAt, or a word in its place.

ran.description: What ran: job.json as the export carries it, and the harness the manifest names.

spec.description: job.json as written, not read through defaults, so a redacted field reads "[redacted]". Its defaults are the ones schema/job/v1.json gives.

harness.description: The adapter that ran, from the manifest.

harnessExit.description: The harness's exit code, from the manifest.

stoppedAtBudget.description: Whether the time budget stopped the harness, from the manifest.

session.description: The harness's name for the conversation this run was a turn in, or "none" for a one-shot job.

outcome.description: What the gate decided, and the state the server holds.

state.description: state.json's state: queued, running, passed, failed or interrupted. A word in its place when state.json is not in the export.

gate.description: The gate's verdict from the manifest, or "none" when the job had no gate.

startedAt.description: state.json's startedAt, or a word in its place.

endedAt.description: state.json's endedAt: when a server wrote the final state, which is not always when the run ended. A word in its place when not held.

finishedAt.description: When the manifest was written, which is when the run ended.

changed.description: What the run changed, from out/diff.patch.

patch.description: The patch's path inside the export, or a word in its place.

sha256.description: The patch's hash as the manifest holds it: the run's own, even when the export carries a redacted copy.

files.description: The paths the patch changes, read from its headers, or a word in their place.

model.description: Which model: asked for, answered at, and paid for with which credential.

asked.description: job.json's model, or "the harness's default" when the job names none.

endpoint.description: The address the harness talked to, from the manifest. Empty when the harness needs no model.

credentials.description: The names of the credentials the proxy added, from out/proxy.jsonl. Never a key. A word in their place when the job did not go through the proxy.

registry.description: The versions of the organisation's model registry the job's model calls were sent under, from out/proxy.jsonl. Empty for a deployment with no registry. A word in its place when the job did not go through the proxy.

spend.description: What the job spent. The harness's report is a claim; the proxy's count is the model calls that left the box, measured from the provider's answers. A call a spending cap refused never left and is counted apart.

tokens.description: The tokens the harness reported, from the manifest, or "not recorded" when it reported none.

costUsd.description: The cost in US dollars the harness reported, or "not recorded".

proxyCalls.description: The model calls out/proxy.jsonl records as sent: not refused by a cap, and not to another host. A word in their place when there is no record.

proxyBytes.description: The response bytes of those calls, or a word in their place.

proxyTokens.description: The input and output tokens the provider reported for those calls. "not measured" when an answer carried no usage, never zero in its place.

proxyUsd.description: What those calls cost in US dollars, priced by the proxy. "not measured" when a call could not be priced, never zero in its place.

refusedCalls.description: The calls a spending cap refused. They sent nothing and cost nothing.

outbound.description: The requests to hosts other than the model, from out/proxy.jsonl, as host:port. They are not model calls and cost no model money.

reached.description: The hosts the job was let through to, or a word in their place.

denied.description: The hosts the job asked for and was refused, or a word in their place.

by.description: The approver. "not recorded": an agent opens a pull request and a person merges it on the forge.

why.description: Why the approver is or is not known.

requests.description: The lines of the server's request log whose path names this job, as the log wrote them, from requests.jsonl. "not recorded" when no log was given to the export.

evidence.description: The manifest the export verifies against.

manifest.description: The manifest's path inside the export: out/manifest.json.

signer.description: Who signed out/manifest.json, as the exporter's keyring checked it: the keyring's name for the key, never the manifest's own signer field. Where no keyring vouched for a name it holds words instead: "unsigned" (there is no out/manifest.sig), "signed, not checked: no keyring", "signed, not checked: key <id> is not in the keyring", or "signed, and the signature does not hold". A verifier derives it again with its own keyring and reports both answers when they differ.

files.description: How many files the manifest names.

carried.description: Every file in the export except this one, with its hash as exported, sorted by name.

name.description: The file's slash path inside the export.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file as exported, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

covered.description: Whether the run's own manifest vouches for these exact bytes. False for state.json, requests.jsonl and every redacted copy, which the export alone vouches for.

redactions.description: Every file the policy dropped or rewrote. Empty when it changed nothing.

file.description: The file's slash path inside the export.

action.description: dropped: the file is not in the export. rewritten: values inside it were replaced.

rules.description: The rules that changed it: "drop <pattern>", "field <name>" or "pattern <name>".

original.description: The hash the manifest holds for the file, so a person with the original can match it to the run, or "not recorded" for a file the manifest does not cover.

policy.description: The retention and redaction policy the export was written under, whole.

drop.description: Files of the export, as slash paths or path.Match patterns, that are not retained. job.json and out/manifest.json cannot be dropped.

fields.description: JSON member names whose values become "[redacted]" in every JSON and JSON-lines file.

patterns.description: Regular expressions replaced by "[redacted: <name>]" wherever they match text.
